title: Large-leaved Lime: Ancient Summer Lindens You Can Visit
meta_description: One lime has marked the point where three Brussels communes meet since 1777. Seven old limes mapped, from Antwerp and Prague to Munich and Vienna.
intro: A lime has marked the exact spot where three Brussels communes meet since at least 1777, and that is the sort of job this species keeps getting: boundary post, landmark, the tree a place organises itself around. Munich protects one of these in law for its bizarre growth, which is an unusual reason to make a tree a natural monument. Prague has one a president refused to lose, Tomas Garrigue Masaryk having had a castle terrace built around it. Telling a large-leaved lime from a small-leaved one is harder than it sounds, and under Nuremberg's 400 year old tree the sign and the botanists who have looked at its leaves still disagree. Seven are mapped across six cities, among them an Antwerp linden protected since 2010 for precisely where it stands rather than for anything rare about the tree itself.
